transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29
Time: 15:00 - 16:00 UTC
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Redwood CSM), Dr. Priya Menon (Aurelia CISO), Tom Baker (Aurelia Procurement), Sofia Ruiz (Aurelia Head ML Ops), Ethan Cole (Aurelia Legal), Jamal Harris (Aurelia Infra)

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood, I'll kick us off. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Tom Baker: Tom here, procurement.
[00:15] Dr. Priya Menon: Priya here, CISO.
[00:18] Sofia Ruiz: Sofia, ML Ops.
[00:20] Ethan Cole: Ethan, legal.
[00:22] Jamal Harris: Jamal on infra.
[00:25] Marcus Chen: Marcus, solutions eng, nice to meet you all.
[00:28] Aisha Patel: Aisha, customer success, happy to coordinate onboarding.

[00:35] Lena Ortiz: Great, goal for today is to walk through the MSA/DPA redlines you sent, talk SLAs, and confirm pricing appendix and next steps for onboarding. Marcus will cover a quick tech note on dedicated vs hosted for the SLA ask.

[01:05] Ethan Cole: Before we dive, quick note from legal: main concerns are liability cap, data residency assurances, and a clearer incident notification timeline in the MSA. The DPA needs to reflect our scope - controlled health data, so stronger processing terms and subprocessor disclosures.

[01:35] Marcus Chen: Understood. On the SLA side, we saw your note on p99 < 150ms for inference. Just to set expectations, that depends on model choice and whether you're on hosted multi-tenant or dedicated GPU pool. Dedicated with pinned model variants + quantization can get closer to that p99, but cost will be higher.

[02:05] Sofia Ruiz: For our customer use cases, p95 around 50-60ms is ideal for patient-facing features. We can tolerate slightly higher p99 for batch tasks, but the ambulatory portal needs predictability.

[02:30] Jamal Harris: We are leaning to a private VPC deployment or at least dedicated capacity in our region due to PHI concerns. We want to ensure keys are customer-managed (KMS) and audit logs shipped to our SIEM.

[03:00] Lena Ortiz: That's totally doable. Our Private offering supports customer-managed KMS and routeable audit logs. For hosted we have SOC2 and encryption-at-rest, but for PHI we typically recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll capture exact language for KMS and log retention in the DPA appendix.

[03:40] Ethan Cole: On indemnity and liability cap: your standard language pins it to amounts paid in last 12 months; our finance team wants a higher cap - or at least carve-outs for data breach.

[04:10] Marcus Chen: From an SE perspective we can commit to operational SLOs and fallbacks. For example, automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant if capacity spikes. That helps availability but won't change contractual liability wording.

[04:50] Dr. Priya Menon: We also need an explicit data residency clause - certain records must remain in our EU region. Can Redwood guarantee region-specific storage and processing?

[05:15] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we offer region pinning for both Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we can pin requests to a region but storage and longer-term logs might be in adjacent regions unless Private is used. We'll specify residency options in the DPA appendix.

[05:45] Tom Baker: Pricing question - your pricing appendix shows usage-based per token and then a dedicated reserved capacity price. We need clarity on how overage is billed and whether we can convert usage to committed capacity credits. Also, volume discounts at scale.

[06:10] Marcus Chen: We support transition: usage credits can be applied to a reserved commitment under a 30-day notice; overage on a reserved plan is billed at reduced overage rates. I'll share a short spreadsheet with example scenarios.

[06:40] Sofia Ruiz: For billing alignment, can we get per-route cost breakdowns? Our teams want to see per-model and per-feature token use.

[06:55] Aisha Patel: Yes, Console offers token-level cost and latency breakdowns and per-route dashboards. We'll share screenshots in the follow-up.

[07:10] Ethan Cole: Back to MSA, there's a clause around subcontractors/subprocessors - need a process to approve new subprocessors and notice before onboarding. The DPA should include a list of current subprocessors.

[07:35] Lena Ortiz: We'll attach the current subprocessors list. For changes, standard 30-day notice is typical; we can discuss an approval process for critical subprocessors.

[08:05] Jamal Harris: Technical question - how do you handle KV cache and multi-tenant leakage concerns? We need assurance that inferences and KV caches are completely isolated per tenant.

[08:30] Marcus Chen: KV cache is isolated per tenant on Dedicated and Private. On hosted, we use strict namespaces and encryption to prevent cross-tenant exposure but we understand that for PHI Dedicated/Private is preferred. There was a note in your doc about cache eviction policy - that affects cold-start latency.

[09:00] Dr. Priya Menon: Incident notification: we require a 24-hour initial notification for security incidents, followed by a detailed report within 5 business days. Can you reflect that?

[09:20] Lena Ortiz: We can insert that timeline; our standard is 48 hours for initial notification but we can mirror the 24-hour ask for high-severity incidents. We'll flag that as a redline to discuss.

[09:45] Tom Baker: SLA credits - how are they calculated? We need a transparent credit formula for availability and latency misses.

[10:05] Marcus Chen: Typically credits are pro-rated percentage of monthly bill based on minutes of SLA violation. For latency SLOs we tie it to percent of requests exceeding p99. We'll provide a sample calculation.

[10:40] Ethan Cole: Please avoid broad service credits that could be gamed. We want a clear definition of measurement windows and excluded maintenance windows.

[11:10] Lena Ortiz: Agreed, we'll propose measurement windows and scheduled maintenance carve-outs.

[11:25] Sofia Ruiz: On onboarding, what is the timeline once MSA signed? We have a pilot we want to run in Nov - two months window?

[11:40] Aisha Patel: Typical timeline is sign, then onboarding kickoff within one week, environment provisioning (VPC/dedicated pool) 1-2 weeks, integration and SSO 1-3 weeks depending on customer resources, then pilot. So two months is reasonable.

[12:05] Jamal Harris: For SSO, we use SAML via our identity provider. Are there any special attributes Redwood expects?

[12:20] Marcus Chen: We support SAML and OIDC, standard attributes like email, name, groups; we'll share our SSO integration doc and a sample metadata file.

[12:45] Dr. Priya Menon: Compliance - do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001? Any penetration testing reports or attestations?

[13:05] Lena Ortiz: Yes, SOC2 Type II available, plus our security pack with pen test summaries and third-party certs. We'll share the security docs link.

[13:25] Ethan Cole: One other legal ask: customer audit rights. We want the ability to audit subprocessors and controls annually. Is that supported?

[13:45] Lena Ortiz: We allow attestation and document reviews; direct on-site audits of Redwood data centers are not supported for hosted, but for Dedicated/Private we can discuss a more detailed audit clause. We'll mark that for legal redline.

[14:10] Tom Baker: Regarding the DPA, please add the specific retention limits and deletion guarantees for PHI after contract termination.

[14:30] Marcus Chen: For Private deployments we can guarantee data destruction per your policy; for hosted we'll provide retention settings and deletion APIs and documented timelines.

[15:00] Ethan Cole: Also, we need clarity around subcontracted cloud providers and where logs reside.

[15:20] Lena Ortiz: We'll include a cloud provider appendix and a logs location matrix.

[15:40] Sofia Ruiz: On pricing again, if we commit to 12-month reserved capacity, can we lock pricing? Our finance needs predictability.

[16:00] Marcus Chen: Yes, reserved capacity contracts come with a committed rate and a discount over on-demand pricing. Multi-year discounts and annual true-ups are available. We'll include an example appendix.

[16:25] Jamal Harris: Network egress - we need to estimate monthly egress for budgeting. Is there a formula?

[16:40] Marcus Chen: Egress depends on token size and response length; we'll run an estimate using your current prompt sizes if you share sample payloads. I'll include a spreadsheet template.

[17:05] Dr. Priya Menon: Encryption - data in transit and at rest yes, but can we require HSM-backed keys for certain workloads?

[17:25] Lena Ortiz: HSM/KMS integrations are supported in Private deployments. We'll note the option and the appendix for key rotation and ownership.

[17:50] Ethan Cole: On indemnity carve-outs for data breach, we may request a non-limited liability for willful misconduct and gross negligence. That is pretty standard, but flag it.

[18:10] Lena Ortiz: Noted. We'll include Redwood's standard language and highlight the carve-outs for negotiation.

[18:40] Tom Baker: Can we get an updated MSA with our redlines tracked? We'll need time to loop back with finance and legal.

[18:55] Lena Ortiz: Yes, I'll send a redlined MSA and DPA with tracked changes by Friday.

[19:10] Aisha Patel: I'll schedule the onboarding kickoff tentative for two weeks after sign and prep a checklist.

[19:30] Marcus Chen: For the benchmark, I'll spin up a dedicated pool in our staging region and run a p95/p99 report with your representative model (Sofia's team to share model choice). Expect results within a week.

[19:50] Sofia Ruiz: We'll share model artifacts and a sample prompt set by tomorrow.

[20:05] Lena Ortiz: Great. Any other open items?

[20:10] Ethan Cole: Just to confirm timelines: redline by 2026-10-01, Marcus benchmarks by 2026-10-04, legal confirmation 2026-10-06.

[20:20] Lena Ortiz: Correct. We'll recap.

[59:00] Lena Ortiz: Recap of action items and close - thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and attach the security pack and pricing scenarios.
[59:20] Tom Baker: Thanks all.
[59:25] Dr. Priya Menon: Thanks.
[59:30] Meeting ended.
